title: Hello World
description: The classic first Java program that prints a greeting to the console.
output: Hello, Java!
explanation: Every Java program needs a class with a main method. System.out.println() writes a line of text to the console.

title: Simple Calculator
description: Takes two numbers and an operator from the user and performs the calculation.
output:
Enter first number: 10
Enter operator (+ - * /): +
Enter second number: 5
Result: 15.0
explanation: Scanner reads user input. A switch statement chooses the arithmetic operation based on the operator character.

title: Even or Odd
description: Checks whether a number entered by the user is even or odd.
output:
Enter a number: 7
7 is Odd
explanation: The modulus operator (%) returns the remainder of division. Any number divisible by 2 with no remainder is even.

title: Largest of Three Numbers
description: Finds and prints the largest among three numbers entered by the user.
output:
Enter three numbers: 4 9 6
Largest number: 9
explanation: Math.max() compares two values at a time, so nesting it lets us compare three numbers in one expression.

title: Leap Year Checker
description: Determines whether a given year is a leap year.
output:
Enter a year: 2024
2024 is a Leap Year
explanation: A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, unless it is also divisible by 100 but not 400.

title: Multiplication Table
description: Prints the multiplication table for a number entered by the user.
output:
Enter a number: 5
5 x 1 = 5
5 x 2 = 10
...
5 x 10 = 50
explanation: A for loop repeats the multiplication ten times, incrementing the multiplier each iteration.

title: Factorial of a Number
description: Calculates the factorial of a number using an iterative loop.
output:
Enter a number: 5
Factorial of 5 = 120
explanation: The factorial of n is the product of all positive integers up to n. A long is used to avoid overflow for larger values.

title: Fibonacci Series
description: Prints the Fibonacci sequence up to a given number of terms.
output:
Enter number of terms: 8
0 1 1 2 3 5 8 13
explanation: Each Fibonacci number is the sum of the two preceding numbers, starting from 0 and 1.

title: Prime Number Checker
description: Checks whether a given number is a prime number.
output:
Enter a number: 29
29 is Prime
explanation: A number is prime if it has no divisors other than 1 and itself. Checking up to its square root is enough.

title: Prime Numbers in a Range
description: Prints all prime numbers between two numbers given by the user.
output:
Enter start and end: 10 30
11 13 17 19 23 29
explanation: The prime check runs inside an outer loop that walks through every number in the range.

title: Palindrome Number
description: Checks whether a number reads the same forwards and backwards.
output:
Enter a number: 12321
12321 is a Palindrome
explanation: The digits of the number are reversed one by one and compared with the original number.

title: Armstrong Number
description: Checks whether a number equals the sum of its own digits each raised to the power of the digit count.
output:
Enter a number: 153
153 is an Armstrong Number
explanation: 153 = 1^3 + 5^3 + 3^3. Each digit is raised to the power of the total number of digits, then summed.

title: Reverse a Number
description: Reverses the digits of a number entered by the user.
output:
Enter a number: 6789
Reversed number: 9876
explanation: The last digit is extracted with % 10 and appended to the result, then removed from the number with / 10.

title: Sum of Digits
description: Calculates the sum of all digits of a number.
output:
Enter a number: 4526
Sum of digits: 17
explanation: Each digit is peeled off the end of the number using % 10 and added to a running total.

title: Number Guessing Game
description: The computer picks a random number and the player tries to guess it with hints.
output:
Guess a number (1-100): 50
Too low!
Guess a number (1-100): 75
Correct! You guessed it in 2 attempts.
explanation: Random.nextInt(100) generates a value from 0-99, so adding 1 gives a range of 1-100. A do-while loop keeps asking until the guess matches.

title: Rock Paper Scissors
description: A simple console game of Rock, Paper, Scissors against the computer.
output:
Choose Rock, Paper or Scissors: Rock
Computer chose: Scissors
You win!
explanation: The computer's choice is picked randomly from an array. The winner is decided by comparing the two choices against the classic rules.

title: Simple Quiz Game
description: Asks a set of multiple-choice questions and keeps score.
output:
Capital of France?
paris
Correct!
...
Your score: 3/3
explanation: Questions and correct answers are stored in parallel arrays. Each user answer is normalized and compared to the expected answer.

title: Tic Tac Toe
description: A two-player console Tic Tac Toe game with a 3x3 board.
output:
- - -
- - -
- - -
Player X, enter row and col (0-2):
explanation: The board is a 2D char array. After every move, rows, columns and diagonals are checked for three matching symbols.

title: Hangman Game
description: A console word-guessing game where the player has limited wrong guesses.
output:
Word: ____  Attempts left: 6
Guess a letter: j
Word: j___  Attempts left: 6
explanation: Correctly guessed letters are revealed in a char array while wrong guesses reduce the number of attempts left.

title: Digital Clock
description: Displays the current system time and updates it every second.
explanation: SimpleDateFormat converts the current Date into a readable time string, printed once per second using Thread.sleep().

title: Unit Converter
description: Converts a length value between kilometers and miles.
output:
Enter distance in km: 10
10.00 km = 6.21 miles
explanation: Multiplying kilometers by the conversion factor 0.621371 gives the equivalent distance in miles.

title: Temperature Converter
description: Converts a temperature between Celsius and Fahrenheit.
output:
Enter temperature in Celsius: 25
25.0 C = 77.0 F
explanation: The formula F = C * 9/5 + 32 converts a Celsius reading into its Fahrenheit equivalent.

title: Currency Converter
description: Converts an amount from US Dollars to Indian Rupees using a fixed exchange rate.
output:
Enter amount in USD: 100
$100.00 = ₹8320.00
explanation: The USD amount is multiplied by a fixed exchange rate to compute the equivalent value in rupees.

title: Student Grade Calculator
description: Calculates a student's average marks and assigns a letter grade.
output:
Enter number of subjects: 3
...
Average: 82.33, Grade: B
explanation: Marks for each subject are summed and divided by the count to get the average, which is then mapped to a letter grade.

title: Student Management System
description: A class-based system to add and display student records in memory.
output:
How many students? 2
...
Roll | Name | Marks
1 | Aarav | 88.0
2 | Diya | 91.5
explanation: Each student is modeled as an object of the Student class, stored in an ArrayList and displayed with a custom method.

title: Bank Account Management
description: Simulates deposit, withdrawal and balance check for a bank account object.
output:
Starting balance: 1000.0
After deposit: 1500.0
Insufficient balance!
Final balance: 1200.0
explanation: Encapsulation keeps the balance field private, only allowing it to change through the deposit and withdraw methods.

title: Contact Management System
description: Stores and searches contacts by name using a HashMap.
output:
Search contact name: Aarav
Aarav's number: 9876543210
explanation: A HashMap stores name-to-number pairs, giving fast lookup of a contact's phone number by name.

title: Library Management System
description: Manages a small book catalog, allowing books to be issued and returned.
output:
Effective Java issued successfully.
Effective Java is already issued.
Effective Java returned successfully.
Effective Java issued successfully.
explanation: Each Book object tracks its own issued status. The catalog is a map from a book ID to its Book object.

title: ATM Simulation
description: Simulates ATM operations: balance check, withdrawal and PIN validation.
output:
Enter PIN: 1234
Enter amount to withdraw: 1000
Withdrawal successful. Remaining balance: 4000.0
explanation: The PIN is validated first; only then is the withdrawal processed against the available balance.

title: Employee Management System
description: Calculates employee salary with bonus using inheritance.
output:
Rahul's salary: 30000.0
Priya's salary: 60000.0
explanation: Manager extends Employee and overrides calculateSalary() to add a bonus, demonstrating inheritance and polymorphism.

title: Expense Tracker
description: Records expenses and prints a total and category-wise summary.
output:
Food: 1200.0
Travel: 800.0
Books: 500.0
Total expenses: 2500.0
explanation: A LinkedHashMap keeps categories in insertion order while accumulating a running total of all expense values.

title: To-Do List
description: A console to-do list that lets the user add and view tasks.
output:
Your To-Do List:
1. Learn Java Collections
2. Practice 5 coding problems
3. Build a mini project
explanation: An ArrayList stores the tasks in the order they were added, and a loop prints them with a running number.

title: Inventory Management System
description: Tracks product stock levels and updates them as items are sold.
explanation: getOrDefault() safely reads current stock, and the map is updated only when there is enough stock to fulfill a sale.

title: File Handling Notes Manager
description: Writes notes to a text file and reads them back using Java I/O.
output:
Java is platform independent.
Streams simplify collection processing.
explanation: try-with-resources automatically closes the writer and reader. Notes are written line by line and then read back.

title: Mini Banking System
description: A multi-account banking simulation supporting transfers between accounts.
output:
Transferred 1500.0 from Aarav to Diya
Aarav: 3500.0
Diya: 3500.0
explanation: Accounts are stored in a map keyed by account ID. A transfer debits one account and credits another only if funds are sufficient.

title: Array Sorting (Bubble Sort)
description: Sorts an array of integers in ascending order using the bubble sort algorithm.
explanation: Bubble sort repeatedly swaps adjacent elements that are out of order until the whole array is sorted.

title: Binary Search
description: Searches for a target value in a sorted array using binary search.
output: Found at index 5
explanation: Binary search repeatedly halves the search range by comparing the target with the middle element of a sorted array.

title: Matrix Multiplication
description: Multiplies two 2D matrices and prints the resulting matrix.
explanation: Each cell of the result matrix is the dot product of a row from the first matrix and a column from the second.

title: String Reversal
description: Reverses a string entered by the user without using a built-in reverse method.
output:
Enter a string: Java
Reversed: avaJ
explanation: The string is traversed from the last character to the first, appending each one to a StringBuilder.

title: Palindrome String Checker
description: Checks whether a string reads the same forwards and backwards.
output:
Enter a string: level
Palindrome
explanation: The string is lowercased and stripped of spaces, then compared with its reversed form.

title: Word Frequency Counter
description: Counts how many times each word appears in a sentence.
output:
java: 3
is: 3
simple: 1
powerful: 1
popular: 1
explanation: The sentence is split into words, and a HashMap keeps a running count for every distinct word.

title: Anagram Checker
description: Checks whether two strings are anagrams of each other.
output: Anagrams
explanation: Two strings are anagrams if their characters, once sorted, are identical to each other.

title: Custom Stack Implementation
description: Implements a basic stack (LIFO) using an array, with push, pop and peek operations.
output:
Top element: 30
Popped: 30
New top: 20
explanation: A stack follows Last-In-First-Out order. push() adds to the top, pop() removes from the top, and an index tracks the current top.

title: Custom Queue Implementation
description: Implements a basic queue (FIFO) using Java's LinkedList as the underlying structure.
output:
Processing: Task 1
Processing: Task 2
Remaining in queue: [Task 3]
explanation: A queue processes items in First-In-First-Out order. poll() removes and returns the item at the front of the queue.

title: Linked List Implementation
description: Builds a simple singly linked list from scratch and traverses it.
explanation: Each Node holds a value and a reference to the next node. Traversal follows the next references until reaching null.

title: Exception Handling Basics
description: Demonstrates catching a runtime exception with try-catch-finally.
output:
Error: Invalid array index - Index 5 out of bounds for length 3
Execution finished.
explanation: The try block attempts risky code, the catch block handles the specific exception, and finally always runs afterward.

title: Custom Exception
description: Defines and throws a custom checked exception for invalid ages.
output: Caught: Age must be 18 or above.
explanation: A custom exception class extends Exception to represent a domain-specific error, thrown explicitly when a rule is violated.

title: Multithreading Basics
description: Runs two threads concurrently that print numbers independently.
output:
Thread-A: 1
Thread-B: 1
Thread-A: 2
...
Both threads finished.
explanation: Extending Thread and overriding run() defines the task each thread performs. start() launches them concurrently and join() waits for completion.

title: Runnable Interface Example
description: Creates threads using the Runnable interface instead of extending Thread.
output:
Worker-1: 1
Worker-2: 1
Worker-1: 2
...
explanation: Implementing Runnable as a lambda separates the task logic from the Thread class itself, which is the preferred modern approach.

title: JDBC Connection Basics
description: Shows the standard pattern for connecting to a MySQL database using JDBC.
output:
Aarav - 88
Diya - 91
(Depends on the actual database contents)
explanation: DriverManager.getConnection() opens a connection to the database, and a Statement runs SQL queries against it, returning rows in a ResultSet.
